headline: Multiomics and machine learning link immune programs to disease genetic risk
label: Genetic Risk And Multiomics
summary: Integrative omics, Mendelian randomization and imaging genetics now connect immune and fibrotic cell states to vascular, neural and disc disease.
synthesis: The shared thread is human-derived multi-omics, single-cell profiling and genetic inference used to localise specific cell states and signalling axes within disease risk. Imaging-genetics and Mendelian randomization anchor part of this set: a GWAS of deep-learning splenic MRI features identifies 219 loci including 9p21 for coronary artery disease, and MAFF is nominated as a possible protective factor in Parkinson's disease. Others prioritise targets through transcriptomic integration, including ELF2 in vascular dementia, ITGBL1 and RPN1 in a fibrotic nucleus pulposus subpopulation, and Spp1-integrin signalling in spinal cord injury fibrosis. A transitional senescent monocyte state is linked to inflammatory monocyte expansion in aging, and influenza vaccination is discussed as a trained-tolerance lens on inflammaging. The novelty lies in resolving bulk associations into cell states and imaging phenotypes; the set is heterogeneous, so this describes a dominant pattern rather than a mechanism common to every item.
